summary: This CSS file styles a data visualization or list interface with controls, a canvas area, and grouped item listings. It uses CSS custom properties (variables) for theming, includes responsive adjustments for mobile devices, and respects user preferences for reduced motion animations.

explanations.20: The `composes` keyword pulls in styles from a global CSS class called `mk-eyebrow` and merges them with the styles defined here — it's a way to reuse styles from elsewhere.
explanations.28: `font-family: inherit` makes this element use the same font as its parent, rather than using the browser's default form font.
explanations.30: `letter-spacing: 0` explicitly removes any letter spacing that might have been inherited from parent styles.
explanations.40: `outline: none` removes the browser's default focus ring so the component can use a custom one below with the box-shadow.
explanations.50: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` makes numbers all the same width so they don't shift around when they change — useful for counters.
explanations.87: The `[open]` selector targets `<details>` elements when they're expanded, so you can style them differently in their open vs. closed state.
explanations.93: `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr))` creates columns that are at least 240 pixels wide but grow to fill space, and automatically adds more columns as space allows.
explanations.98: `min-width: 0` overrides the browser's default `min-width: auto` for grid items, allowing content to shrink below its natural width if needed.
explanations.131: In the mobile media query, `flex-direction: column` stacks the controls vertically instead of horizontally.
explanations.141: `white-space: normal` allows text to wrap on mobile, undoing the `white-space: nowrap` set earlier for desktop.
explanations.147: This removes the `transition` animation for users who've enabled reduced motion in their accessibility settings, respecting their preference.
